title: Yara and the Protocol
premise: Dominic Voss, caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, has kept the colony invisible for three years by hauling cargo through contested orbits — until the colony's children, led by a girl named Yara, begin sharing an identical dream that turns out to be a compressed transmission from the enemy fleet's own conscripted children. The message contains proof that both sides' leadership manufactured the war to justify the jump-gate monopoly, and it must be broadcast through the contested relay before the jump window closes in nine days. Dominic and Yara must choose between the protocol of silence that has kept them alive and the truth that could end the war; they broadcast it, and the war fractures — not into peace, but into something more dangerous and more honest: two fleets that now know their children on both sides were dreaming the same dream.
about_author: Casper Ashgrove is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for satellite networks before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable internet and strong opinions about seed banks.

chapters.title: The Quiet Orbit
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A routine cargo haul past the derelict seed vault establishes the colony's fragile invisibility: no transmissions, no lights, no names on any manifest. Dominic returns to find the children silent at dinner, all staring at nothing. Emotional beat: the unease of a man who has built his life on routines that suddenly feel like a held breath.

chapters.title: Yara Counts to Nine
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Ten-year-old Yara, the colony's unofficial archivist, interviews each child and discovers their dreams are identical down to the smell of ozone and a countdown: nine days. The adults dismiss it as mass hysteria. Emotional beat: a child's loneliness when she sees something true that grown-ups refuse to look at.

chapters.title: What the Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Searching the seed vault's legacy systems for an explanation, Dominic finds the dream's imagery matches an encrypted packet logged three years ago — the night the previous caretaker died. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing, and the first crack in his belief that staying invisible was ever a choice rather than a sentence.

chapters.title: The Consensus of Children
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On day seven of the countdown, the dreams sharpen into words: coordinates, a relay frequency, and a phrase in a dead language Yara recognizes from her archive work. She convinces the other children to help her decode it in secret. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of conspiracy, and loyalty forming between kids who've never had anything to hide before.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest, Redacted
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A routine inspection by a neutral trade authority nearly exposes the colony; Dominic realizes someone in the fleet command already knows where they are and is choosing, for now, to look away. He decodes half the children's message: evidence the war's opening strike was staged. Emotional beat: vertigo — the survival protocol he serves may be built on a lie.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Dominic confronts Yara; she shows him the full decoded message, including its origin: children aboard the enemy flagship, conscripts like them, broadcasting on hope alone. The colony council votes to destroy the data and hold the silence. Emotional beat: heartbreak — duty and love pulling the same people in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Theft of Small Things
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. With the council sealing the archives, Yara and two friends smuggle the message core out inside a seed canister from the vault — hiding truth in the one place Earth still trusted to keep things alive. Dominic catches them, and instead of stopping them, helps. Emotional beat: the moment a caretaker decides what he is actually caring for.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The haul to the relay becomes a gauntlet: patrol drones, a boarding scan, and a hail from the enemy flagship asking, in a child's voice, whether they received the dream too. Dominic answers honestly for the first time in three years. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into resolve as invisibility ends mid-flight.

chapters.title: Broadcast Before the Window Closes
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, climax. At the relay, with minutes left in the jump window and a fleet interceptor closing in, Yara keys the transmission while Dominic burns their cargo as chaff and decoy. The message goes out to both fleets simultaneously. The interceptor holds fire. Emotional beat: the raw, suspended instant between action and consequence — love spent against duty, and winning by seconds.

chapters.title: After the Dreaming Stops
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue. The dreams cease. The war doesn't end neatly — fleets splinter, councils fall, negotiations begin ugly and real — but ships on both sides now answer to their children's names. The colony lights its windows for the first time. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope; identity reclaimed, survival redefined as something more than staying hidden.
